case.background: A pickup coil is connected to a sensitive galvanometer inside a controlled magnetic field. The meter responds during a field change but returns to zero when the field is steady. Infer the law governing the peak response magnitude.
initial_observations: A steady field produces no sustained meter deflection.
Changing the field produces a transient voltage whose dependencies are not given.

controls.description: Number of turns in the aligned pickup coil.
controls.name: coil_turns

controls.description: Area enclosed by each turn of the pickup coil.
controls.name: loop_area_cm2

controls.description: Magnitude of the uniform magnetic-field change through the coil.
controls.name: field_change_mt

controls.description: Time over which the magnetic-field change occurs.
controls.name: change_time_ms

instruments.description: Interchangeable aligned pickup coils, a controlled electromagnet field ramp, a timer, and a high-impedance galvanometer.
instruments.name: induction_coil_galvanometer

notes: The field is uniform and normal to every turn; resistance does not load the voltage readout.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'faraday_flux_change_power_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain exactly reference_emf_mv, turn_exponent, area_exponent, field_change_exponent, and change_time_exponent.

readouts.description: Magnitude of the peak induced electromotive force.
